text: Partly it's because they didn't grow up with it, so things that seem obvious to young people, like swiping or tapping an icon, aren't natural to them. Apps also change their design so often that just when someone has learned where a button is, it moves. I think a lot of older people also worry about making a mistake they can't undo, which makes them avoid experimenting.

tips.en: Partly, also, also add reasons one after another.
tips.kk: Partly, also, also — себептер бірінен соң бірі қосылады.
tips.ru: Partly, also, also — причины добавляются одна за другой.
tips.example: Apps also change their design so often

tips.en: Fear of mistakes is a psychological reason and shows insight.
tips.kk: Қателесуден қорқу — психологиялық себеп, терең естіледі.
tips.ru: Страх ошибки — психологическая причина, звучит глубоко.
tips.example: worry about making a mistake they can't undo

note.en: “Did not have it when they were young”.

questions.question: Why do older people sometimes find new technology difficult?

text: I'd say it's done both. On the practical side, things like online banking and delivery apps save us hours of queuing and travelling. On the other hand, because we're always reachable, it's much harder to switch off. Many people check work emails in bed or on holiday, which means the stress of the job never really stops. So technology removes some pressures but creates new ones.

tips.en: I'd say it's done both is an honest answer to an either-or question.
tips.kk: I'd say it's done both — «не-не» сұрағына шынайы жауап.
tips.ru: I'd say it's done both — честный ответ на «или-или».

tips.en: Emails in bed and on holiday prove the second point.
tips.kk: Төсекте және демалыста хат тексеру екінші жағын дәлелдейді.
tips.ru: Письма в постели и в отпуске доказывают вторую сторону.
tips.example: Many people check work emails in bed or on holiday

phrases.text: removes some pressures but creates new ones

questions.question: Has technology made people's lives less stressful or more stressful?

text: I think the basics should be taught, yes, but not because every child will become a programmer. Coding teaches you to break a big problem into small, logical steps, which is useful in almost any field. At the same time, I'd be careful not to replace other subjects with it. Children still need art, history and sport just as much as they need digital skills.

tips.en: Not because … shows the real reason coding matters.
tips.kk: Not because … — сөйлеуші код шын мәнінде не үшін керек екенін нақтылайды.
tips.ru: Not because … — говорящий уточняет, зачем на самом деле нужен код.
tips.example: not because every child will become a programmer

tips.en: At the same time, I'd be careful adds a limit and balances the view.
tips.kk: At the same time, I'd be careful — шектеу ұстанымды салмақты етеді.
tips.ru: At the same time, I'd be careful — ограничение делает позицию взвешенной.
tips.example: I'd be careful not to replace other subjects with it

questions.question: Should children be taught to code at school?

text: The most obvious risk is that data can be leaked or stolen, and then things like phone numbers or card details end up in the wrong hands. But there's also a less visible risk: companies build detailed profiles of us and use them to influence what we buy or even what we believe. The worrying thing is that most people accept the terms without reading a single line.

tips.en: The most obvious … but also a less visible … moves from simple to complex.
tips.kk: The most obvious … But there's also a less visible … — қарапайымнан күрделіге.
tips.ru: The most obvious … But there's also a less visible … — от простого к сложному.

title.en: An obvious and a hidden risk

tips.example: But there's also a less visible risk

tips.en: The worrying thing is gives an emotional but precise evaluation.
tips.kk: The worrying thing is — эмоционалды, бірақ дәл баға.
tips.ru: The worrying thing is — эмоциональная, но точная оценка.
tips.example: The worrying thing is that most people accept the terms

phrases.text: end up in the wrong hands

questions.followUp: Do people care enough about privacy?
questions.question: What are the risks of sharing personal data with apps?

text: In some areas, I think they do. A handful of companies now decide what billions of people see in their news feeds, and that gives them enormous influence over public opinion. Their products are genuinely useful, of course, so I'm not suggesting we stop using them. But I do think governments need clearer rules about how these companies use data and what they're allowed to promote.

tips.en: A handful … billions shows how big the problem is.
tips.kk: A handful … billions — қарама-қайшылық мәселенің көлемін көрсетеді.
tips.ru: A handful … billions — контраст показывает размер проблемы.
tips.example: A handful of companies now decide what billions of people see

tips.en: Of course … But I do think admits the positives, then gives a firm view.
tips.kk: Of course … But I do think — артықшылықты мойындау, сосын анық пікір.
tips.ru: Of course … But I do think — признание плюсов, затем чёткое мнение.
tips.example: But I do think governments need clearer rules
